questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
Since the exchange was only for half a year, I wanted to go somewhere where I knew I could communicate with the locals. Thus, it was important for me to go to an English speaking country. As I have already lived in North America for 4 years, Oceania was an obvious option for me. Furthermore, I have always dreamed of going to Australia and saw this as the perfect opportunity. 

The choice of city that I wished for in Australia depended on what each university had to offer. In the preparation process, I spent a lot of time looking at what classes each university offered. Here I found that Melbourne, and in particular Monash University, had the best options for my interests.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I have really enjoyed my exchange semester in Melbourne and I would encourage everyone, who has the opportunity to go on exchange, to do so. You grow a lot as a person by living in a foreign country.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very easy. Monash University offers a pick up service at the airport which I had signed up for. Thus, upon arrival I just called the driver, and he took me to where I was staying the first few days.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Before the semester began, all exchange students had to attend an orientation day at Monash where they explained us a bit about Australian culture, Monash as an institution and how and where we could seek help if we needed any. Furthermore, they had a bunch of activities for all Monash students where you could learn more about Australia, do fun activities with other students, or learn about the different clubs an societies that Monash University offered.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was actually a bit difficult to find accommodation. Due to covid, many rental agencies had downscaled the amount of rental properties they had. Thus, being the first batch of exchange students after several years of lockdown, the demand for housing was a lot higher than the supply. However, I still managed to find a great place that I shared with some other exchange students.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I would suggest that you talk to other exchange students about which neighbourhoods you live in. If you live somewhere close to others, it makes it a whole lot easier to meet up. Melbourne is a big city and it can take a while to get from one point to the other, so having others close to you will make your experience a lot more fun. I was lucky to find a complex where a bunch of different exchange students lived as well.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The market was not good but this was mainly due to the lockdown during the pandemic where Australia was hit really hard. I do not believe that this is still the case anymore but since we were the first exchange students to come after they reopened the country, the industry was not yet back on track. Many of the rooms that were available were quite nasty so it took a bit of time to find a nice place that fit my cleaning standards.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process was super easy. A few days after arriving, I just went to Monash Connect (the student service center), got my student id and then that was it. It took around 10-15 minutes in total.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The employee at Monash Connect was very friendly and helpful. After making my id, he helped me understand how to read my schedule and unfortunately also gave me the news that 3/4 of my classes were online. At first I was very sad about it, but as soon as the semester started, I became quite happy with it because it gave me a lot more flexibility that I would've otherwise had. Additionally, it did not at all affect my chances of making new friends as I was initially worried about.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was fortunate to get into all 4 classes that I wanted to. After arriving at Monash, I wanted to change one of my classes to another one (one that I had also gotten a pre-approval for from KU) and this process was also very smooth. The employee at Monash Connect helped me apply for the other class, and a few days later, I was registered for that one instead.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Ask for help if there is anything you are not sure about. The people at Monash Connect are really friendly and they are there to help you. It can be a bit overwhelming coming to a new university and figuring out all the processes and terminology, so just asking about the things you don't understand is really my best advice.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I really enjoyed the courses I took at Monash. They were so interesting and very applicable (not theory heavy).

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
The level of the courses varied quite a bit. I took one course on the Australian economy and one on the Chinese economy, and these two courses were essentially the same except from the fact that they focused on two different economies. However, their structure and evaluation processes were very similar. They required quite a lot of reading but they were not difficult courses. For both courses, the teachers also explained to us that they were not meant to be difficult but rather to bring new perspectives and help students understand how each economy works. I really enjoyed both classes and even though it was a lot of readings, I did not mind it as it was very interesting. 

Then I also took an accounting class called Business Analytics and the level in this class was really low. Even though I've only taken one other accounting class in my entire life, I was able to easily pass this class without spending much time on it throughout the semester. Thus, it was really not demanding and I would not say I learned a lot from it, but it was nice to have one easy class when my other three classes were so demanding. 

Lastly, I took an introduction to programming in Java class and this was by far the most difficult class for me. I probably spent around 60% of my study time on this class. As an economics student it was also a bit optimistic to take a class in software development. Nonetheless, I absolutely loved this class. I learned so much from this class. My teacher was super good and our three TAs were so helpful. Without them, I am not sure I would've gotten through this class. The level was very high and on average 20% of the students in the class fail. But if you put an effort into it, you get 10x back from taking this class.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There are a lot more evaluations throughout the semester in Australia. For example, your assignments will count towards your final grade, you will have a midterm, sometimes weekly quizzes as well as a final exam. Your grade for the class will then be affected by all of those evaluations. I think this is very different from KU where your exam is everything. The way it is structured in Australia makes it more demanding as you cannot slack throughout the semester if you want a good grade. On the other hand, your grade will not be depending on one thing and on you being on your best on the certain day of the exam.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
At Monash, I took the following classes:
- ACF5320: Business Analytics
- ECX5631: The Australian Economy
- ECX5630: Chinese economy and global business
- FIT9131: Programming foundations in Java

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would highly recommend The Australian Economy and Chinese Economy and Global Business. I really enjoyed those classes and you cannot find anything similar at KU. Furthermore, they are not too difficult to pass. I think the level is very good when you're an exchange student - you learn a lot but you still have time to explore the city as well.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: If you go on exchange in Melbourne as a master student, beware that you cannot get a discount on the local transportation as bachelor students can. This means that local transportation can quickly become very expensive. Student organisations have fought for discounts to grad students for more than 20 years but still without luck. Note that this is only for cities in the state of Victoria. All other states in Australia have discounts for grad students as well.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Flight tickets were a lot more expensive than I expected. Food was also more expensive than I expected but this might have been due to the inflation as a result of the pandemic which many countries have experienced.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were a lot of different clubs available. I cannot remember all of them but I know they had an association for grad students where they sometimes organised events. They also offered different sports clubs i.e. tennis, swimming etc., outdoor clubs, a club for Australians as well as foreigners who are interested in exchanges and many others.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I lived quite far from the campus and therefore I did not take part in any clubs. You can certainly still take part in clubs even if you decide to live far from campus, but for me I just had so many other things to do. The unfortunate thing about Monash is that their campus (at least Clayton campus which is the big one) is about an hour from downtown. Thus, many exchange students chose to stay closer to the city instead. It was not a problem at all as the public transportation system in Melbourne is quite good.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would definitely recommend that you do the Great Ocean Road. Furthermore, Wilson's Promontory is also very beautiful and worth a weekend trip. There are also a lot of activities going on in Melbourne and you can easily find several activities to fill up your weekend with in the city. There are several accounts on instagram that you can follow to get tips on what's going on in the city and surrounding areas such as "whatsonmelb" and "nathsway".

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was extremely easy for me. I did not have the slightest feeling of culture shock but I have also lived in North America for 4 years and Denmark the rest of my live. Australia is a good mixture of North America and Europe, so it felt like home for me.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Don't be afraid to talk to students in your class. It can be hard to make friends with the locals because they already have friends, family and maybe a job they need to pay attention to. But Australians are very friendly and they'd be happy to talk to you.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None just all the insects and animals haha.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Australians are nice and friendly and the coffee is absolutely amazing. Seriously, at least in Melbourne, you find excellent coffee on every street corner - and enjoy the coffee while you're there because you won't find the same quality when you get back home. The best coffee I've ever had was from Studio Beans in St Kilda.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Go with an open mind and a positive attitude and I promise you it will be an amazing experience. The two weeks before the semester starts are extremely important as this is where you have a chance to meet other students. Take advantage of this and make sure you attend as many events as possible. Do not be afraid to approach people and ask them where they are from. There are a lot of exchange students from Denmark, the Netherlands and Germany in Australia, so you will find many people who come from a similar culture as you.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Choose your classes wisely. Decide what you want to get out of your exchange semester: whether you want to take challenging classes where you will learn a lot or if you would rather take easier classes that allows you to have more time for other things. Do your research well and beware that at Monash there are quite a lot of courses that do not have a final exam. If you are smart, you can choose only courses with no final exam.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding part was to get to live in Australia and learn about the Australian culture. It was really amazing. Sharing the experience with so many other exchange students was also really nice as well as taking classes that taught me things I could've not taken back home.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: In the beginning I found it very hard to find my group of people. I wanted to have some people that were as close as my friends back home but that takes time. Some of the others did find friends that they became extremely close to but I did not. Nonetheless, I accepted that that was also ok. I have two large groups of people that I could always reach out to to do fun activities with. I came to accept that for the time I was in Australia, it was very ok to not have any very close friends but having many that I got along with well and could have a good time with was also amazing.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Go go go! I can only give my best recommendations to go on exchange and in particular go to Australia. It was amazing.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
